The ceiling here is a depth arm, the floor is a depth arm, and the whole bet is whether the strikeout shape holds enough through the levels to keep that K-BB% propped up once the walks stop being cheap.

834962_hitter.text: Seventeen home runs across AA & A+ in 370 plate appearances, with 48 walks against 79 strikeouts, is a bat-first first baseman profile that carries real weight at Double-A. The .218 ISO translates to .156 against MLB pitching, and the translated 10.2% walk rate clears the MLB average of 8.5%, so the approach adds something even after the level discount. A 13% walk rate and .378 OBP suggest someone who can put a lineup together rather than just feast on minor-league arms. If the contact, 21% strikeouts and .266 average, survives the jump, DePino is a low-end everyday regular at first; if it doesn't, the power alone leaves a useful bench bat.

834978_pitcher.text: The surface numbers are loud: 11.0 K/9, a 1.1 WHIP, a K-BB% that ranks 90th among the pitcher pool across AA & A+. Translate those 96 innings to MLB-equivalent context and the profile goes quiet fast, with a K/9 of 8.5 sitting right at league average and a BB/9 of 3.6 that runs a tick above it. The stuff plays up in the minors in a way it probably won't against a big-league lineup. If the command tightens and the strikeout rate holds its shape at that level, he's a backend arm who eats innings; if neither translates, what's left is a depth piece competing for a roster spot.
